result.result:
The app is built. It runs with `npx @angular/cli@19 serve`, and logging in with `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard. The production build finishes with no warnings.

I tested it in a headless browser at 1280×900:
- **Login:** empty-field errors appear, and sign-in and sign-out both work.
- **Profile menu:** it opens leftward and stays fully on screen (it ends at x=1216 in a 1280px viewport). It closes on an outside click.
- **CRUD:** edit, invite, delete from a row, delete from inside the edit dialog, and backdrop/Escape closing all work, and the table updates each time.
- **Console:** no errors.

Every page and dialog uses the design-system components, and styles use only the tier-2 decision tokens: no hex values, no tier-1 or tier-3 variables.

The project wasn't scaffolded, so I generated an Angular 19 app into the folder. The `node_modules` I found had Angular 21 in it, so I reinstalled.

## Where the spec and Figma disagree
The Figma data loaded fine, but it differs from the spec in a few places. Where they conflict, I followed the spec for content and Figma for layout and proportions:
- **Login card:** Figma also shows a "Blueprint" title and a divider line. I left both out because the spec says "add nothing else".
- **Dashboard:** Figma has different numbers and service names; I used the spec's. There is no separate Data Summary tile in Figma, so I put it next to System Logs on a third row (4 + 8 of 12 columns). The "System Overview" heading and "Last updated" line are in Figma, so I kept them.
- **Log viewer:** Figma shows it as a styled list, but the spec asks for a terminal look in a monospace face, so it's a dark monospace panel.
- **Users table:** Figma combines avatar and name into one "User" column; I kept them separate as the spec's columns do. Figma styles Edit as the plainest button and Details as outlined; I followed the spec, so Details is plainest and Edit is outlined. Joined dates show as "Jan 2024", as in Figma.
- **Header:** Figma's "Online" badge is left out. I used "Dashboard" and "Team Members" as nav links instead of Figma's four placeholder links, which have no pages.

## Workarounds
- **Header profile control:** `dsb-header` has no slot for extra content, so the avatar, name and menu sit on top of its right edge.
- **Role dropdown in dialogs:** `dsb-modal` clipped the open Role menu. One global rule in `src/styles.css` lets the menu overflow only while it is open. It targets the library's internal class names, which could break in a future release.
- **Header and footer links:** these components render plain links, which reload the page. I send in-app links through the Angular router instead.

## Design choices with no token
The token set has nothing for these, so I either left them out or used the closest value:
- **Fonts:** there's no font token. Inter (the Figma font) is set once in `src/styles.css`, and the log viewer uses a generic monospace stack.
- **Card shadows:** Figma's card shadows are left out, since the only shadow tokens are for menus and modals. Cards have a border only.
- **Borrowed sizes:** there are no height tokens, so the chart and log viewer heights reuse layout-width tokens. Large sizes use the nearest step: 26px values render at 22px and 12px corners at 10px.
- **Breakpoints:** the dashboard's two media queries use plain pixel values, because CSS variables can't be used in media queries.

The built-in dialog chrome also follows the library rather than Figma: no divider lines, 540px wide instead of 560px, and slightly different padding.
